text.p: Swiss shares took a slide near the end of the session to end a rangebound and quiet session slightly lower.
Dealers said the lack of follow-through buying and the reluctance of investors to take positions ahead of Friday's U.S. jobless data led the market down after initial gains.
The Swiss Market Index of leading shares lost 7.1 points, or 0.2 percent, to close at 3,627.1 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index ended down 9.33 points, or 0.4 percent, closing at 2,325.91.
Roche certificates, which led the actives list, continued to be pressured, falling 65 francs to 8,975. The certificates lost ground on Wednesday after a Merrill Lynch downgrade.
Sulzer registered shares recovered slightly from early losses, but still closed six francs lower at 722.
The machine producer reported a markedly higher 1996 first half net profit on Wednesday, but troubles at its textile machine division and a cautious outlook turned investors off, a trader noted.
Utility firm Elektrowatt soared seven francs to 491 on recurring rumours that CS Holding was about to sell its 45 percent Elektrowatt stake, one dealer said.
CS Holding fell 0.81 percent to 123. UBS slid five francs to 1,153.
Among insurers, Swiss Re advanced three francs to 1,297.
Food giant Nestle temporarily fell below a important level of 1,390 francs. The shares ended dow six francs to 1,393.
